(1) Area One has the vast majority of blight and contains the largest number of people: (It should be noted that in terms of density, Area Two has approximately the same density but constitutes a much smaller area.) This area is composed almost entirely of residential use, occasional corner stores comprise the commercial uses, and public and semi-public uses consist of several churches and one school. The residential structures are generally of frame construction. Rows of decaying wooden structures covered with asphalt shingles are common. Many structures are heated with oil or wood burning stoves. Overcrowded conditions are the rule. Children play in the streets or alleys, or in vacant lots that have collected abandoned cars or debris. The streets are congested and often dangerous to pedestrians. Idlewood Avenue is a congested street extensively used by through traffic. Heavy trucks and construction equipment are common as well as school buses and children on bicycles. A commercial strip in Meadow Street between Rosewood Avenue and Grayland Avenue creates traffic congestions and parking problems. Little parking space is provided creating hazardous automobile-pedestrian conditions in addition to those present on Idlewood Avenue. This situation combined with heavy litter and trash accumulation make this strip incompatible with residential use.
Other conditions in Area One are unpaved alleys that create dusty or muddy areas, and serve as litter, garbage, and junk collectors. Open lots and built up areas adjacent to alleys often create pockets of accumulated trash, abandoned cars, and overgrown dry vegetation. The composite of these ingredients create a condition prime for vermin, rodents, and fire hazards. Some buildings in this area are "concrete-block cells", cubes made of concrete blocks with minimum sized windows, dirt front yards, no sidewalks, no landscaping, no offstreet parking, no play space, and no maintenance. Many streets are without sidewalks. Many areas are poorly lighted. Many areas are considered dangerous to walk through not only for outsiders but community residents as well. The physical environment of Area One constitutes the largest area of blight and blighting conditions and it is continually growing larger as it spreads block to block.
